new_statements.quote: [p.109] Otras aves de corral, tales como el 'ganso' y el 'pavo', reciben nombres tomados del castellano con las consiguientes adaptaciones fónicas; son bastante comunes las formas gansu y pafu y en la isla Huapi, donde predomina la acentuación oxítona, se encuentran las variantes gansú y pafú. [...] [n.3, p.113] Por otra parte, se recurre a la tilde únicamente para destacar las variantes agudas características de los hablantes de la isla Huapi; en lo demás, se sigue la norma del alfabeto unificado.
new_statements.translation: [p.109] Other farm birds, such as the goose and the turkey, receive names taken from Spanish with the corresponding phonic adaptations; the forms gansu and pafu are quite common, and on Isla Huapi, where oxytone (final) accentuation predominates, one finds the variants gansú and pafú. [...] [n.3] Moreover, the written accent is used only to highlight the oxytone variants characteristic of the Isla Huapi speakers; otherwise the norm of the Alfabeto Unificado is followed.
new_statements.citation: Contreras, Constantino. 1990. Palabras claves del mundo huilliche: observaciones sobre léxico y etnografía. Alpha (Osorno) 6: 103-118.
new_statements.locator: p. 109 (section 9, aves de corral) and note 3, p. 113
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Copies checked (all under, present and consistent): 16 pp = Alpha 6: 103-118, image-only, ilovepdf producer) +; . Quote check (Contreras 1990): I rendered PDF page 7 (printed '- 109 -') and page 11 (printed '113') and read them directly. p.109: 'Otras aves de corral, tales como el 'ganso' y el 'pavo', reciben nombres tomados del castellano con las consiguientes adaptaciones fonicas; son bastante comunes las formas gansu y pafu y en la isla Huapi, donde predomina la acentuacion oxitona, se encuentran las variantes gansu' y pafu'.' -- verbatim as reported (the scanned textidentical). p.113 n.3: 'Empleamos aqui las grafias del alfabeto unificado mapuche con las leves adaptaciones para el area…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Only a partial, sub-variety statement exists: among Isla Huapi (Lago Ranco) Huilliche speakers final-syllable (oxytone) accentuation predominates and is flagged as a local peculiarity; for the rest (San Juan de la Costa tsesungun) accent is left unmarked as following the general Mapuche norm, i.e. implicitly the pan-Mapudungun pattern (penult in vowel-final words, final in consonant-final words, per Lenz p.388 n.1 / Salas), which no source states for Huilliche in so many words. Lenz (p. XXIV, with Huilliche examples s'úka ~ s'uká-mo) adds that the accent is weak and positionally unstable, shifting with phrase rhythm.
new_statements.exceptions: Contreras marks non-final accents on some cited forms despite n.3 (súngoll 'olla', pútriwe 'colgador de ollas', kúsuf 'viento') alongside final ones (fotúm, mawún, kuú, ketrú, gansú, pafú); Lenz notes disyllables vary by position in the phrase (s'úka vs s'uká-mo).
new_statements.domain_note: Contreras: lexical citation forms from elicitation interviews (San Juan de la Costa, Isla Huapi, Rupumeica etc.), statement restricted to Isla Huapi speakers. Lenz: word accent described as weak and dependent on 'el ritmo del conjunto' (phrase rhythm) - arguably phrase-level conditioning.
new_statements.identity_note: Contreras 1990's positional statement concerns the Isla Huapi (Lago Ranco, Provincia de Ranco) sub-variety of Huilliche, which he contrasts with the San Juan de la Costa (Osorno coast) variety = tsesungun/chesungun, the core huil1244 variety; both fall under huil1244 (no separate glottocodes). Lenz 1895-97's accent remarks are framed for 'araucano' in general but sit inside the introduction to his Huilliche text (Estudio I, speaker Domingo Quintuprai of Osorno) and use Huilliche example forms (s'uka = ruka). The Alvarez-Santullano et al. 2016 RLA study covers Lanco, Panguipulli, Maihue, Rupumeica and Aleucapi (Los Rios/Los Lagos 'territorio huilliche'), partly transitional to central Mapudungun (mapu1245).

new_statements.quote: [p. 6, Estudio I, huilliche] En el empleo de los acentos no he sido riguroso; el acento en jeneral en araucano no es fuerte, i fluctúa sobre diferentes sílabas de la palabra segun el ritmo del conjunto; jeneralmente he pintado el acento solo cuando me parecia tener cierta fuerza o una posicion no comun. [p. XXIV] El acento tiene poca fuerza i poca estabilidad; a menudo cambia su lugar segun leyes poco fijas de equilibrio; por ejemplo: Təfámu məlei ñi s'uka (aquí está mi casa) pero: ñi s'uká-mo kəpán (de mi casa vengo). [p. 388 fn. 1] En jeneral se observa hasta hoi la regla establecida ya por el Padre Valdivia que las palabras araucanas se acentúan en la penúltima; solo cuando terminan en consonante suelen ser agudas.
new_statements.translation: [p. 6] In the use of accent marks I have not been rigorous; in general the accent in Araucanian is not strong, and it fluctuates over different syllables of the word according to the rhythm of the whole; I have generally marked the accent only when it seemed to me to have a certain force or an uncommon position. [p. XXIV] The accent has little force and little stability; it often changes its place according to scarcely fixed laws of balance; for example: Təfámu məlei ñi s'uka (here is my house) but: ñi s'uká-mo kəpán (from my house I come). [p. 388 fn. 1] In general the rule already established by Father Valdivia is still observed today, that Araucanian words are stressed on the penultimate [syllable]; only when they end in a consonant are they usually oxytone.

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record for Huilliche has an empty rule; Lenz supplies an explicit general-Araucanian rule (penult; final if consonant-final) and a strong qualification that the accent is weak and phrase-rhythm-dependent. His Huilliche-specific remark (p. 6, note prefacing Quintuprai's Osorno Huilliche text) is only that the accent is weak and fluctuates; the penult/final-if-closed rule is stated for 'palabras araucanas' in the Cantos section (Moluche/Pehuenche material), not for Huilliche as such. Against the existing statement (Contreras 1990: oxytone accentuation predominates on Isla Huapi, e.g. gansú, pafú), Lenz's rule would predict paroxytone stress for vowel-final words, so there is parti…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The only explicit rule Lenz gives (p. 388 fn. 1, in the Cantos section, stated for Araucanian in general) is: stress the penultimate syllable, except that consonant-final words are stressed on the final syllable, i.e. a closed final syllable attracts stress. But everywhere he touches the subject, including the note prefacing the Huilliche text of Domingo Quintuprai (p. 6), he insists the accent is weak and unstable, moving across syllables with the rhythm of the phrase and with suffixation (p. XXIV: s'uka vs. s'uká-mo; p. 388: 'el acento mismo varía de una sílaba a la otra cuando la añadidura de sílabas finales cambia la configuracion de la palabra'). Pehuenche note 320 (p. 171) adds: 'El acento en araucano no tiene lugar fijo ni en las palabras tomadas del castellano.'
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing explicit on secondary word stress. In sung verse (p. 388) he notes a mostly trochaic rhythm, with occasional clashes of two adjacent stressed syllables and lapses of two or three unstressed syllables, and says these observations are provisional.
new_statements.exceptions: Consonant-final words are oxytone (p. 388 fn. 1). Stress shifts with the phrase and with added suffixes (s'uka / s'uká-mo, p. XXIV). Spanish loanwords often take proparoxytone instead of paroxytone stress (p. 171 n. 320, Pehuenche section). Lenz states he marked accents only where they seemed strong or in an unusual position (p. 6), so the marks in the texts are not a systematic record.
new_statements.identity_note: Lenz's Huilliche material is the dialect of Domingo Quintuprai of Osorno (Estudio I, elicited in Santiago) plus the Estudio II dialogues and the short Huilliche pieces of Estudio IV; the explicit stress rule (p. 388 fn. 1) and note 320 (p. 171) are stated for Araucanian in general or in the Pehuenche/Moluche sections. Lenz's own view (p. XXIII-XXIV) is that Huilliche is the most divergent of the dialects, mainly through devoicing of fricatives and laterals, and he notes no accentual difference between Huilliche and the other dialects.

readall_conflicts: Within Lenz the statements are in tension rather than contradiction: he says in three places that Araucanian accent is weak, unstable and 'no tiene lugar fijo' (pp. XXIV, 6, 171, 388), yet the single explicit rule (p. 388 fn. 1) is penultimate stress with final stress on consonant-final words, and Molineaux 2014 finds his actual accent marks conform to that rule (penultimate mora) in every dialect including Huilliche. Between sources: the existing Contreras 1990 statement that oxytone accentuation predominates on Isla Huapi (gansú, pafú, vowel-final oxytones) does not match Lenz's general rule, but the two describe different Huilliche communities (Osorno 1890s vs. Isla Huapi 1980s) and Lenz's rule is stated for Araucanian in general, not for Huilliche specifically.
